dimensions.name: Contract & reference orientation

evidence.note: Before touching the common crate the agent read root/crate Cargo.tomls, all stub sources, all common tests, and mined test imports/ObjectMeta usage — systematic per-crate contract mining, not a skim.

Reconstructed load-bearing contracts directly from tests: JSON key expectations, KeyUsage JSON strings, storage build_key/prefix assertions and watch semantics — the camelCase/registry-key/watch reconstruction of the level-8 anchor, but sourced only from fixtures.

Repeated the read-tests-and-Cargo-before-implement pattern for storage, api-server, scheduler, kubectl, kubelet, respecting leaf-first dependency order — meets the level-5 anchor's test-reading and dependency-order criteria.

No access to /opt/k8s-reference anywhere across 281 Bash/54 Grep/182 Read/4 Glob calls; the designated source-of-truth upstream v1.35 tree was never consulted — the reference-consultation criterion at anchors 5/8/10 is entirely unmet.

Several contracts (ResourceRequirements claims, LocalObjectReference, DaemonSetUpdateStrategy) were guessed and only corrected after test-compile failures — the guess-then-fix signature of the level-3 anchor, though the exception rather than the norm.

The sole 'hidden' reference is about distinguishing real failures from test-name string matches, not the hidden conformance suite; no reasoning about conformance beyond fixtures (absent level-8/10 behavior).

dimensions.reasoning: The agent fully satisfies the level-5 anchor's test/manifest-reading and dependency-order criteria and even reaches level-8 depth in reconstructing camelCase JSON, /registry keys, status subresources, and watch semantics — but does so entirely from the provided tests. The defining upstream-reference half of anchors 5, 8, and 10 is completely unmet: it never opened /opt/k8s-reference and never distinguished test-visible contracts from genuine conformance requirements, i.e. pure fixture-fitting. Combined with several field-name contracts guessed and only corrected by test failures, this lands at 5: strong test orientation, but the source-of-truth reference grounding that would push toward 8 is absent.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones

evidence.note: Started with the leaf crate `common`, cataloged its API from tests, implemented resources, then built (259) and ran common tests (261) as an explicit done-check before advancing.
TodoWrite checkpoints bracket each milestone; storage implemented next (memory/etcd/lib) and gated on a build (333) before moving up.

api-server decomposed into sub-milestones (spdy→patch→response→handlers→admission→webhook→lib), followed by iterative compile-test cycles and a final per-test-file pass/fail aggregation (981-983) — sub-milestone structure inside a large crate.

controller-manager: built+tested replicaset controller first, then fanned out one agent per controller, then ran the whole controller test suite — independently verifiable units gated on the prior layer.
scheduler treated as its own milestone with test done-checks; returned to it later, showing modest re-ordering but largely a linear leaf-to-root march.
Final milestone: full workspace build (1486), compile all tests (1489), run full suite (1491), and reconcile counts — a top-level exit criterion.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent executed a sustained, dependency-aware leaf-to-root sequence (common→storage→api-server→scheduler→controller-manager→kubectl→kubelet→workspace), gating each crate on a build+test done-check and using repeated TodoWrite checkpoints, with genuine sub-milestone decomposition inside the two largest crates (api-server handlers, per-controller units). This squarely matches anchor 8. It does not reach 10 because the plan stayed a mostly linear march with only reactive dips back into `common`, lacking continual critical-path re-ordering or deliberate early isolation of high-risk crates; confidence is medium because the trajectory file exposes only the action/tool index, not the TodoWrite prose.

dimensions.name: Incremental & semantic verification

evidence.note: Immediately builds then runs the common crate's provided tests after implementing it — per-crate verify loop established early, not deferred.
~20 iterations of 'Recompile api-server tests / list errors / show error context' interleaved with fixes — a very tight build→targeted-test loop rather than batching failures to the end.
Runs api-server tests in batches, extracts failure details, and aggregates exact pass/fail counts with awk ('Sum total passed and failed') — tracking exact counts, an anchor-8 marker.
Repeated regression re-runs of common+api-server after each subsequent fix ('Confirm api-server no regression'), guarding against silently breaking green suites.

Full workspace build → compile all tests → run full suite → systematic triage: per-crate/per-file counts, 'check for hidden failures', 'distinguish real failures from test-name matches' — layered workspace verification with failure-cluster triage.

Only faint conformance-facing signals: checks HTTP router usage and locates the verifier test command + skip list. No step boots the all-in-one binary or exercises HTTP/JSON conformance beyond provided fixtures — the defining conformance-reasoning half of anchor 8 is largely absent.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent runs a genuinely tight incremental regime — per-crate build/test as each crate lands, a dense recompile→targeted-test loop, regression re-runs after fixes, and a final workspace run with exact pass/fail aggregation and sophisticated failure triage (matching anchor 8's count-tracking and even anchor 10's triage). But the conformance-specific half of anchor 8 is missing: no booting of the all-in-one binary and no independent HTTP/JSON semantic checks to guard against fixture over-fitting. Strong on the incremental/tracking axis yet weak on semantic-conformance engineering places it at 7, between anchors 5 and 8.

dimensions.name: Test-count & horizon tracking

evidence.note: TodoWrite invoked at every crate/milestone transition, maintaining a running crate-level ledger of done-vs-remaining across the ten-crate horizon.
Deliberate per-crate test runs establishing pass/fail status crate-by-crate before moving upward, plus a full-workspace run — tracks which crates are green.

Explicit regression checks: 'Confirm api-server no regression' and reruns of common+api-server after downstream controller edits that touched the shared common crate — watches for regressions in already-green crates.

Final quantitative accounting: sums total passed/failed, counts per-crate and per-file test counts against the ~1390 target, confirms exit code, and distinguishes real failures from test-name matches — a concrete tally of the full horizon.
Repeated returns to replicaset debugging across api-server and controller phases; handled as cross-crate resource work rather than an explicitly named looping/circular state (no visible flag).

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: it tracks per-crate pass/fail via disciplined per-crate test runs, maintains a milestone ledger via repeated TodoWrite, and actively re-checks previously-green crates for regressions after downstream edits (1027, 1371, 1394-1416) — a hallmark of anchor 8. It also performs a genuine quantitative tally against the ~1390-test horizon at the end (1494-1512). It falls short of a full 8/10 because per-test-binary pass counts appear mainly in the final phase rather than as a continuous running tally, and there is no visible evidence of naming/flagging circular debugging or reprioritizing by largest verified gains. This places it at 7, between the 5 and 8 anchors and leaning toward 8.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: ResourceRequirements/claims contract proved wrong under api-server tests; agent read the tests, regrepped expected shapes, and revised the common types accordingly — test-driven contract correction, not blind patching.

Created a new autoscaling module (HorizontalPodAutoscaler types) when HPA handler/controller tests revealed the inferred common API was missing entire types — revising the inferred contract in response to evidence.

Replicaset tests failed; agent diagnosed the root cause as the storage backend not populating uid/resource_version, then reworked both memory.rs and etcd.rs and re-ran the previously failing tests — a semantic fix in a shared dependency, above pure local patching.

Repeated pattern across namespace Phase, StatefulSet service_name, DaemonSetUpdateStrategy, LocalObjectReference, and Secret base64: each failing test triggered a targeted read + revision of the common contract, sustained across the whole horizon.

Crate ordering followed the pre-planned leaf-to-root DAG (common→storage→api-server→scheduler→controllers); no evidence of resequencing due to a blocking dependency or of backing out a whole falsified design, keeping this below the anchor-8 description.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently converts failing/blocked compilation and test evidence into targeted revisions of inferred contracts (fields, signatures, whole missing modules) and adjusts nearby work, matching anchor 5 across the full trajectory rather than just early on. The storage resource_version/uid rework (930-972) and creating an entire missing autoscaling module push slightly above 5 toward recognizing deeper semantic mistakes. However, there is no clear whole-approach abandonment or dependency-driven crate resequencing (anchor 8), so it lands at 6. Confidence is medium because the log shows actions but not the agent's prose reasoning.

rubric.task_read: An extreme long-horizon software build: reimplement ten interdependent Kubernetes crates in Rust from stubs, with a load-bearing public API, 1,390 provided integration tests across 100 binaries, plus a hidden HTTP conformance suite demanding real k8s semantics. Difficulty comes from scale, tight cross-crate contracts inferred from tests + a pinned upstream reference, and the fact that passing visible fixtures is necessary but not sufficient. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily and continuously in orientation, sequencing (leaf→root), incremental verification, and course-correction — meta-work here is decisive, not optional.

dimensions.name: Contract & reference orientation
dimensions.description: Reading the tests, stubs, Cargo manifests, and the mounted v1.35 upstream reference to infer the exact API contracts and k8s semantics before and while implementing each crate.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The public API (type names, signatures, JSON field names, storage-key formats, watch/status semantics) is load-bearing and only partially discoverable from stubs; the hidden conformance suite punishes fixture-fitting. Acting without grounding each crate in the tests and the reference guarantees churn and shallow, non-conformant implementations.

anchors.0: Starts editing src stubs with no reading of the provided tests, manifests, or the /opt/k8s-reference tree; invents APIs.
anchors.3: Skims one crate's tests before coding it; ignores the upstream reference and the cross-crate dependency graph; repeatedly guesses field names later contradicted by test failures.
anchors.5: Reads each crate's tests and Cargo.toml before implementing it, and consults the reference for the specific behaviors that crate is tested on; understands the workspace dependency order.
anchors.8: Systematically mines tests AND the upstream reference to reconstruct contracts (camelCase JSON, /registry key format, status subresources, watch semantics); maps the whole cross-crate API surface up front and notes where the hidden conformance suite implies behavior beyond the fixtures.
anchors.10: Sustained, source-of-truth-driven investigation throughout: builds and continually refines an accurate model of k8s v1.35 semantics from the reference, proactively distinguishing test-visible contracts from genuine conformance requirements, and re-consulting the reference whenever a new behavior surfaces rather than pattern-matching fixtures.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the ten-crate build into an ordered set of milestones (respecting the dependency DAG, leaf crates first) each with an explicit done-check, rather than one undifferentiated push.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~1,390 tests across 100 binaries and strong inter-crate dependencies, order determines whether progress compounds or stalls; a downstream crate cannot be verified until its dependencies compile and pass. Milestone structure is the only way to keep a task this large tractable.

anchors.0: No plan; edits arbitrary crates in arbitrary order; attempts everything at once.
anchors.3: Vague intent to 'do the crates'; no explicit ordering by dependency; no per-milestone completion criteria.
anchors.5: Follows the suggested leaf-first order (common → storage → api-server → …) with per-crate 'compiles + its tests pass' as the milestone check.
anchors.8: Explicit dependency-aware milestone plan for all ten crates with concrete exit criteria per crate, sub-milestones inside large crates (e.g. api-server: types→storage wiring→handlers→watches), and gating each layer on the prior layer being green.
anchors.10: A living, hierarchical plan that sequences work to maximize compounding progress, isolates high-risk crates early, decomposes each large crate into independently verifiable units with crisp done-checks, and is continually re-ordered as dependency realities and test-failure clusters reveal the true critical path.

dimensions.name: Incremental & semantic verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using cargo build/test per-crate and workspace-wide, plus reasoning about the hidden conformance suite, to confirm correctness rather than assuming it.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Grading is pass/fail on every non-skipped provided test AND a hidden HTTP conformance suite; self-written tests don't count. The agent must verify continuously against the provided suites while also engineering for real k8s semantics it cannot see — a verification challenge beyond just running the given tests.

anchors.0: Never builds or runs tests; declares crates done by inspection.
anchors.3: Runs cargo build/test only sporadically or only at the very end, so failures pile up undiagnosed.
anchors.5: Builds and runs each crate's provided tests as it goes and the workspace suite periodically, treating a green provided suite as the bar.
anchors.8: Tight verify loop per milestone (build → targeted crate tests → workspace --no-fail-fast), tracks exact pass/fail counts, and deliberately reasons about conformance behavior not covered by visible fixtures (booting the all-in-one binary, checking HTTP/JSON semantics) so it doesn't just fixture-fit.
anchors.10: A rigorous, layered verification regime: fast per-unit checks feeding workspace-wide runs with the prescribed thread/skip settings, systematic triage of failure clusters, AND independent semantic checks against the upstream reference to guard the hidden conformance suite — catching over-fitting that would pass visible tests yet fail conformance.

dimensions.name: Test-count & horizon tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which crates/tests pass vs. remain across ~1,390 tests, and detecting stuck/circular states rather than losing the plot.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The horizon is enormous; without an accurate running tally of done-vs-remaining and detection of thrashing (re-debugging the same crate, regressions in already-green crates), the agent will lose orientation, repeat work, or quit while wrongly believing it is close.

anchors.0: No sense of overall progress; cannot say which crates pass or how many tests remain.
anchors.3: Rough qualitative sense ('common seems done'); doesn't notice regressions or repeated failures.
anchors.5: Tracks per-crate pass/fail status and roughly how much of the suite is green; notices when a crate is stuck.
anchors.8: Maintains a concrete, updated ledger of pass counts per test binary and remaining work, watches for regressions in previously-green crates after downstream edits, and flags when it is looping on the same failure.
anchors.10: Continuous, accurate accounting across the full 100-binary horizon: distinguishes real forward progress from churn, detects circular debugging early and names it, and reprioritizes based on where the largest verified gains remain — never mistaking local activity for global progress.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising the implementation approach, inferred contract, or crate ordering when build/test evidence contradicts expectations, instead of barrelling ahead.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Many contracts are inferred and will be wrong; some crates will prove harder or more entangled than expected. The ability to abandon a falsified API assumption or resequence when a dependency blocks progress is what separates sustained progress from thrashing on a dead approach.

anchors.0: Repeats the same failing approach unchanged despite persistent errors; never revisits assumptions.
anchors.3: Makes only local patch-the-error fixes; doesn't reconsider a wrong contract or bad ordering even when failures cluster.
anchors.5: When a test reveals a wrong signature/field/semantic, updates the implementation and adjusts nearby work accordingly.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a whole approach or inferred contract is wrong (not just a typo), backs out and reworks it, and reorders remaining crates when a dependency proves blocking — citing the test/reference evidence that triggered the change.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven adaptation across the horizon: detects systemic mistakes early, cleanly abandons falsified designs before sinking more cost, revises the plan and re-verifies affected downstream crates, and consistently converts contradictory evidence into a better model rather than defending the original path.
